subject: Dedicated capacity: transient uplift orchestration for Cobalt Dynamics
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@cobaltdynamics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Dedicated sizing & transient uplift orchestration

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Per our conversation I wanted to capture a short kickoff note and a couple of asks so we can map the Dedicated fleet plan to your Q4 launch profile. Key items for us to validate:

- Expected concurrent sessions at peak and average (you mentioned quarter-over-quarter bursts).
- Typical token mix (user prompts vs system pipelines vs reranks) and average response lengths.
- Acceptable cold-start latency for instances that scale up beyond your reserved slab.
- Any hard constraints on preemption or jobs that must never be evicted (e.g., long-lived fine-tuning).

Could you drop the spreadsheet with the hourly projections (we can use that to sketch headroom bands) and confirm whether you want automatic shoulder capacity (pre-warm) or prefer policy-driven manual bursts?

I've attached a one-page draft of an autoscale policy we often start from; it includes a pre-warm buffer, a fast path for warm-up by priority, and a crediting scheme for transient uplift. Karthik and Hannah are cc'd to help turn this into numbers once we have your projections.

Next step: if you can share the estimates, I'll run a quick simulation and circle back with a concrete reserve + ephemeral plan and suggested SLA addendum language.

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-autoscale-draft.pdf (policy summary, 2 pages)

From: Sophie Li <sophie.li@cobaltdynamics.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Santini <marco@cobaltdynamics.com>
Date: 2028-10-30T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated sizing & transient uplift orchestration

Hi Mateo —

Thanks — attaching the hourly projection workbook (see cobalt_capacity_estimates.xlsx). A few clarifications from our side:

- Baseline: 180 concurrent sessions average (typical weekday).
- Peak: expected short spikes to ~720 concurrent sessions during product demos and marketing pushes, lasting 10-45 minutes, up to 6x baseline on some days.
- Token mix: ~65% user prompts (avg 350 tokens), 25% model-generated content (avg 700 tokens), 10% scoring/rerank (short). Estimated sustained token ingest at true peak ~3.6k tokens/sec.
- Critical workloads: our anomaly-detection batch jobs (nightly) must not be preempted once started — they can run in a separate reserved slab.
- Cold-start tolerance: demo flows need <400ms additional tail latency; we can tolerate occasional 600ms for non-demo bursts.

We prefer as much automatic handling as possible — we don’t want to manually approve small bursts — but we need clear cost controls and a hard cap so the bill doesn't blow out during black-swan traffic.

Let us know if you need anything else — Marco looped in for final procurement constraints.

Best,
Sophie
Head of Product, Cobalt Dynamics
Sophie.li@cobaltdynamics.com

Attachment: cobalt_capacity_estimates.xlsx (hourly projections, 4 tabs)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@cobaltdynamics.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-10-31T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated sizing & transient uplift orchestration

Sophie / team —

Thanks for the detailed projection — this is great. I sketched a pragmatic policy that balances availability, latency, and cost predictability. Summary below; I'll attach a short worked example in the drive link.

Policy proposal (high level):
- Reserved slab: size to cover 1.5x your weekday baseline (we recommend starting with 270 concurrent-equivalent capacity). This keeps your nightly anomaly jobs and steady traffic on guaranteed capacity.
- Shoulder pre-warm: maintain a dynamic pre-warm buffer equal to 0.5x baseline during business hours (automatically kept warm).
- Ephemeral surge pool: allow autoscaling up to 3.0x baseline above reserved slab using ephemeral GPUs. Ephemeral pool will be best-effort, with >90% of excess requests served within the fast-path if warm-up is triggered early.
- Fast warm path: when request queue/moving-average token rate crosses the surge trigger (15% sustained over 60s), we pre-warm N instances in parallel using prioritized cold-start slots (N computed from projected tokens/sec and model latency).
- Hard cap / billing guardrail: configure a per-account hard cap (configurable) to limit ephemeral spend; alerts at 60% and 80% of that cap with auto-throttling fallback to a smaller model variant or queued requests.
- Non-preemptible slab: nightly anomaly jobs run on the reserved slab or a dedicated partition flagged as non-preemptible in orchestration.

Sizing math (short):
- Convert concurrent sessions -> tokens/sec (from Sophie sheet). Example: baseline 180 sessions -> ~1.1k tokens/sec; peak 720 -> ~4.4k tokens/sec.
- Estimate model throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) for your chosen model profile; pick slab such that reserved + shoulder covers typical 95th percentile. Ephemeral covers 99.9th percentile bursts within cap.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a 72-hour shadowing period where the policy is enabled but all autoscale actions are logged (no actual ephemeral allocation), to surface false triggers.
- We can enable a ‘canary warm-up’ for scheduled demos (ad-hoc pre-warm via API) to guarantee <400ms tail.
- For cost transparency, we’ll provide token-level breakdowns and ephemeral spend dashboards; we can also map bursts to HubSpot activity so you can reconcile marketing pushes.

I attached a short PDF that turns the above into a playbook and included an example cost curve. Open questions for you:
1) Do you want ephemeral spend to be deducted from a monthly burst credit bucket, or billed raw per-minute?
2) Any blackout windows (e.g., regulatory maintenance) where autoscale must be disabled?

If acceptable, Mateo and I can produce the SLA addendum language to include the hard cap, billing guardrails, and canary warm-up clause.

–Karthik
Senior Product Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-autoscale-draft.pdf (policy summary attached earlier)

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Li <sophie.li@cobaltdynamics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-01T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Dedicated sizing & transient uplift orchestration

Sophie —

This looks good to me and matches what we discussed. Quick answers to the open questions:
- Bursts: we can offer an optional monthly burst credit (pre-purchased) which caps invoiced ephemeral spend; leftover credits roll forward for one billing cycle. Alternatively, you can choose pure pay-as-you-go with a hard cap we enforce. We’ll include both options in the deal addendum so you can pick.
- Blackout windows: understood — please send any specific maintenance windows and we’ll mark them in the orchestration policy to prevent autoscale.

Next steps: I’ll schedule a short workshop (30–45m) with Karthik and Hannah to walk the team through the playbook and finalize the reserved slab number. Proposed time: 2028-11-03 10:00 PT. Thoughts?

Thanks,
Mateo
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
